## Story Goal

Ensure the CRM has a complete, correctly-authorized, fully-tested SLA Policy administration surface that satisfies CRM-60's acceptance criteria:

1. Managers/Admins can list, create, edit, activate/deactivate, and mark-as-default SLA policies with per-priority targets (first-response minutes, resolution minutes).
2. Agents can read SLA data but cannot mutate policies.
3. Backend enforces validation (positive integers, resolution ≥ first-response, no duplicate priority targets, exactly one active default) and returns i18n-friendly, non-technical errors.
4. Frontend `SlaPoliciesManagementView` covers list / create / edit / activate-deactivate / empty / loading / error states with English LTR and Arabic RTL support.
5. All backend (`SlaPolicyEndpointsTests`) and frontend (`sla.store.spec.ts`, `SlaPoliciesManagementView.spec.ts`) tests pass and cover the edge cases in this story.

**Out of scope** (explicitly deferred to later stories, do **not** touch here):

- SLA timers / breach detection (owned by `SlaEvaluator.cs`, `SlaAutomationHostedService.cs`).
- Escalation rules & dispatcher (`EscalationDispatcher.cs`, `EscalationRuleEndpoints.cs`).
- Notifications, automatic assignment, complex policy matching (segment/branch/product/channel).

## Product rules (from story)

**Existing behaviour (verify — leave unchanged if already correct):**

- SLA policy CRUD is authenticated and authorized.
- Targets stored as integer minutes.
- Each policy scoped to the ticket priorities `Critical`, `High`, `Medium`, `Low` (or whatever `Ticket.cs` already declares — reuse verbatim).

**New/hardened behaviour required by CRM-60:**

- Exactly one policy may have `IsDefault=true` at any time; toggling default on policy A must clear it on any other policy in the same transaction.
- Deactivating a policy that is currently the default must either (a) reject with a friendly error, or (b) clear the default flag as part of deactivation — pick one and document in an endpoint comment; the frontend must surface the resulting toast.
- Existing tickets that already reference a policy must **not** be affected when the policy is deactivated (do not cascade). Verify by grepping `Ticket.cs` for `SlaPolicyId` and confirming no cascade rule.
- Duplicate `(SlaPolicyId, Priority)` rows on a target must be rejected before persistence (validator) **and** by a unique index (defense-in-depth).
- Validation error responses must be structured (400 + problem-details or a machine-readable payload) so the frontend can map to i18n messages such as `"Another default SLA policy already exists."`.

**File:** `backend/CRM.Api/Sla/SlaPolicy.cs`

- Confirm the entity exposes: `Guid Id`, `string Name`, `string? Description`, `bool IsActive`, `bool IsDefault`, `DateTimeOffset CreatedAt`, `DateTimeOffset UpdatedAt`, and a navigation `ICollection<SlaPolicyTarget> Targets`.
- Confirm `SlaPolicyTarget` has: `Guid Id`, `Guid SlaPolicyId`, priority (using the exact type from `backend/CRM.Api/Tickets/Ticket.cs`), `int FirstResponseMinutes`, `int ResolutionMinutes`.
- If any field is missing, add it; if `IsDefault` is absent, add a new EF Core migration in `backend/CRM.Api/Tickets/Migrations/` following the naming convention of `20260825144627_AddSlaPolicies.cs`.

### 2 — DbContext, indexes and unique constraints

**File:** `backend/CRM.Api/Tickets/TicketDbContext.cs`

- In `OnModelCreating`, ensure:
  - `SlaPolicy.Name` has `MaxLength(200)` and a unique index (case-insensitive if the rest of the codebase uses `citext`; otherwise a case-insensitive `HasIndex(...).IsUnique()`).
  - `SlaPolicyTarget` has a unique composite index on `(SlaPolicyId, Priority)`.
  - A **filtered unique index** on `SlaPolicy.IsDefault` where `IsDefault = true` so PostgreSQL enforces a single default (`HasIndex(p => p.IsDefault).HasFilter("\"IsDefault\" = true").IsUnique()`).
- If any of the above is missing, add a new migration (do not edit the existing `20260825144627_AddSlaPolicies.cs`).

### 4 — Endpoints

**File:** `backend/CRM.Api/Sla/SlaPolicyEndpoints.cs`

Verify all five routes exist and are authorized as follows:

| Route | Method | Required permission |
|---|---|---|
| `/api/sla/policies` | GET | `SlaPolicyRead` (Agent + Manager + Admin) |
| `/api/sla/policies/{id}` | GET | `SlaPolicyRead` |
| `/api/sla/policies` | POST | `SlaPolicyManage` (Manager + Admin) |
| `/api/sla/policies/{id}` | PUT | `SlaPolicyManage` |
| `/api/sla/policies/{id}/status` | PATCH | `SlaPolicyManage` |

Inside the handlers, enforce these validations (return `Results.ValidationProblem` / `Results.BadRequest` with an error-code payload the frontend can translate):

- `Name` required, trimmed, `1..200` chars; non-whitespace-only.
- `Targets` contains one entry per priority defined in `Ticket.cs`; reject if any priority appears twice.
- Each `FirstResponseMinutes > 0`, `ResolutionMinutes > 0`, `ResolutionMinutes >= FirstResponseMinutes`.
- On `IsDefault=true`: inside a single `IDbContextTransaction`, `UPDATE SlaPolicy SET IsDefault=false WHERE Id<>@id` before saving the new/updated policy so only one default remains.
- Deactivating (`IsActive=false`) a policy that is currently default: clear `IsDefault=false` on the same policy in the same call and return a warning code (e.g. `"sla.defaultCleared"`) so the frontend can toast.

## Edge Cases & Failure Modes

- **Empty / whitespace-only name** → 400 with `errors.nameRequired`; enforced in `SlaPolicyEndpoints.cs` create/update handlers and mirrored in the Vue form.
- **Duplicate priority in `targets[]`** → 400 with `errors.duplicatePriority`; also blocked by the unique composite index on `(SlaPolicyId, Priority)` in `TicketDbContext.cs`.
- **Zero / negative minutes** → 400 with `errors.firstResponsePositive` / `errors.resolutionPositive`.
- **`ResolutionMinutes < FirstResponseMinutes`** → 400 with `errors.resolutionLessThanResponse`.
- **Extremely large minutes** (e.g. > 525600 = 1 year) → cap in validator with `errors.targetTooLarge`; document the cap in a code comment.
- **Two policies both `IsDefault=true`** → prevented by the filtered unique index; if a concurrent request races, catch `DbUpdateException` on the unique index and translate to `errors.duplicateDefault`.
- **Deactivating the default policy** → clear `IsDefault` and return a `warnings: ["sla.defaultCleared"]` payload for the frontend to toast.
- **No active policy exists** → new tickets are not blocked in this story (SLA timers are out of scope); the list view still renders normally with an "Inactive" badge on all rows.
- **Database failure on save** → catch at endpoint boundary, log, return 500 with `errors.generic`; the store surfaces the shared toast — never leak SQL text.
- **Unauthorized agent hits `POST/PUT/PATCH`** → policy middleware returns 403; store maps to `errors.forbidden`.
- **Existing tickets referencing a deactivated policy** → confirm no cascade in `TicketDbContext.cs`; tickets keep their `SlaPolicyId` and their snapshotted target minutes (if snapshotting was already implemented in CRM-100/101/63 — verify while reading those plans).
- **Arabic RTL** → confirm the Create/Edit dialog and table respect `dir="rtl"` via `useLocale`; visually verify with `?locale=ar`.

## Migration / Rollback

- If new fields (`IsDefault`) or indexes are missing, add a single new migration named `AddSlaPolicyDefaultAndUniqueIndexes` in `backend/CRM.Api/Tickets/Migrations/`. Do **not** edit prior migrations.
- Migration must contain:
  - `AddColumn` for `IsDefault` (nullable → backfill `false` → drop nullable) if the column does not yet exist.
  - `CreateIndex` unique composite on `SlaPolicyTargets(SlaPolicyId, Priority)`.
  - `CreateIndex` filtered unique on `SlaPolicies(IsDefault) WHERE IsDefault = true`.
- Rollback: `Down()` drops the two indexes and (if added) the `IsDefault` column. On a partially-applied state (e.g. duplicate default rows already exist) the unique index creation will fail — the deployment script must first run a de-duplication step keeping the most recently updated default before applying the migration.
